labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/1-causality
labels.notes: chronalMembrane (:163) is a library Causal.Causality (Causal/Causality.lean:77). Its le U is TransGen (membraneStep U), the expression oneWayMembrane uses. chronalMembrane_le is Iff.rfl, and in a probe `chronalMembrane.le = oneWayMembrane.le := rfl` checks. lt U is TransGen (chronalMembraneStep U) (:94). A step is a.1 < b.1 and a.2 < b.2, which is the open future cone in null coordinates (u, v) = (t + x1, t - x1). It also needs segment a b inside U, and a.2 <= a.1 -> b in membraneRight. That is: a step starting in Rbar = {x1 >= 0} ends in R = {x1 > 0}. I read every field. lt_mem_left/right come from the first and last segment. lt_trans is TransGen.trans. lt_mono enlarges U in the segment field. le_of_lt goes step by step: strict gives the product order, and a in R gives a in Rbar, hence b in R. isOpen_lt_right moves the end of the last step (eventually_right: open strict inequalities, R open, the segment kept in U by a thickening of the compact segment). isOpen_lt_left moves the start of the first step (eventually_left). If b is not in R, then a is strictly left, and the open left side keeps the side condition. Nothing is degenerate: lt is non-empty in every open set (chronal neighbours), and lt is not le. Closed form chronalMembrane_lt_top_iff (:204): x <<_M y iff x <_Mink y and (x in Rbar -> y in R). I checked it by hand, by induction on the chain. This is exactly the title's five pairs (left << left, membrane or right; membrane << right; right << right). It is also the evidence's I+(m) = I+_Mink(m) cap R, I-(m) = I-_Mink(m) cap L0, I-(p) = I-_Mink(p) cap L0 for p left, I+(r) = I+_Mink(r) cap R, and full open cones otherwise. chronalMembrane_lt_imp carries the closed form to every U through lt_mono. not_exists_causality_naive_membrane_chronology (:245) says: no Causality C on R x R has C.lt top x y <-> (x <_Mink y and (x in R -> y in R)). That is the timelike analogue of the membrane's own le rule. It is true. p = (0, 1) is strictly left (u < v). Under that rule I-(p) = {y.1 < 0, y.2 < 1, y not in R}. It contains the membrane point (-1/2, -1/2), but none of the points (-1/2 + d, -1/2), which lie in R and in the cone. So I-(p) is not open, against isOpen_lt_left. This is the planner's claim, proved. Disclosed reading (SCOPE, REPORT questions): polygonal chains of future timelike segments stand for 'timelike curves in U that respect the membrane'. 'Respect' is read as: once the curve is in Rbar at a parameter, it is in R at every later one, which is the five pairs along the curve. I re-derived the equivalence. Along a segment x1 is affine, so a chain respects the membrane (pos_affine_of_nonneg). Conversely, take a timelike curve in U (u and v strictly increasing; piecewise C1 with timelike tangent is a special case). Inscribe a polygon on a partition finer than a thickening of its compact image inside U. Each edge is timelike and lies in a convex ball inside U, and the side condition holds at the vertices. So both readings give the same <<_U. The witness is the polygonal causality in any case. The hypothesis row says 'carried, in a reading' while the label is marked: see finding 1.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/2-chronal-neighbours
labels.notes: chronalMembrane_chronalNeighbours states Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours (ladder.toml:346). #print: ChronalPastNeighbours C and ChronalPastNeighbours C.dual. Each says: every v in every open V has p in V with p <<_V v, with the chronology taken in V. The pair is v - (rho/2, rho/4) and v + (rho/2, rho/4), each joined to v by one segment inside a sup-norm ball of radius rho in V. Side conditions: if v - (rho/2, rho/4) is in Rbar, then v.2 <= v.1 - rho/4, so v is in R. If v is in Rbar, then v.2 + rho/4 < v.1 + rho/2. Both hold. The closer's finding is true. At a membrane point m, the diagonal point m - (e, e) lies on the membrane, so it is in Rbar while m is not in R: it is not << m. By the closed form, I-(m) = I-_Mink(m) cap {x1 < 0}. Also m + (e, e) is not in I+(m) = I+_Mink(m) cap R. So both neighbours must be tilted right in time (dx1 = (du - dv)/2 = rho/8 > 0), as the Lean has it. The roadmap block (title and evidence, roadmap.toml:925-937) contains no diagonal pair: see finding 2 on the attribution.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/3-arc-connected
labels.notes: chronalMembrane_causallyArcConnected states Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected. #print: for every U <= top and all p, q, (le U p q <-> some CausalCurveOn U c 0 1 joins them) and (lt U p q <-> some ChronalCurveOn U c 0 1 joins them). So 'for both relations' is the conjunction of the two iffs. The le half is the one-way membrane's own, used unchanged: CausalCurveOn is CurveOn C.le, which is definitionally oneWayMembrane's. The lt half is the delicate step, and it holds. A chronal step is realised by its affine curve (chronalMembraneStep.chronalCurveOn, :320). #print CurveOn: fields mem and rel, local strict increase in every open N <= U about c t. The sub-segment between parameters s < s' stays in a ball inside N, its ends are strictly ordered, and the side condition passes to the sub-segment (pos_affine_of_nonneg, :296, checked by hand). Chains are joined by CurveOn.exists_concat. The converse direction comes from the library through causallyArcConnectedOn_iff. AbsolutelyMinimal (Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal, ladder lean) follows by CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimal (ArcConnected.lean:216). AbsolutelyMinimalOn W holds for every W (ArcConnected.lean:203). #print AbsolutelyMinimalOn: for every cover S of W and every open V <= W, every le_V and lt_V is a TransGen of relations in V inf O, O in S. Its universal closure is the either-reading form (kb/0074, OQ-18).

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/4-tarentin
labels.notes: chronalMembrane_tarentin states Causal.Causality.Tarentin (ladder lean; #print: for every x and every U in nhds x, there are p, q in U with x in openDiamond top p q). It comes from the library's ChronalNeighbours.tarentin (ChronalTarentin.lean:179).

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/5-causally-open-future
labels.notes: CausallyOpenFuture, CausallyOpen (two-sided, DEC-8), LocallyCausallyOpen(Future) and CausallyOpenFutureOn read only J+- (#print: Jplus/Jminus U V), hence only le. le is oneWayMembrane's, so each statement is the audited OneWayMembrane theorem, by defeq: oneWayMembrane_causallyOpenFuture, _not_causallyOpenPast, _causallyOpenPastOn_iff, _not_locallyCausallyOpen. Causally open in the future: yes. Not in the past: chronalMembrane_not_causallyOpenPast states the negation of dual.CausallyOpenFuture. An open set is causally open in the past iff it misses the membrane {u = v}. So the space is neither causally open nor locally so.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/6-not-push-up
labels.notes: chronalMembrane_not_pushUpOn (:429): no open W containing a membrane point m has PushUpOn W (#print: in every U <= W, both halves of push-up, relational form). I checked the witnesses by hand. Let y = (m.1, m.2 + r/2) and z = (m.1 + r/4, m.2 + 3r/4), both in a ball inside W. Then m <=_W y by a null segment; its side condition is vacuous since m is not in R. Next y <<_W z by a timelike segment; y is strictly left, so its side condition is vacuous. But z is strictly left (z.2 > z.1), so m <<_W z would contradict the closed form (m in Rbar -> z in R). This is the evidence's r <= v << w argument at the membrane. not_locallyPushUp follows at (0, 0) (LocallyPushUp = for all x, there is W containing x with PushUpOn W). not_pushUp goes through causal_ladder read backwards: push_up and chronal_neighbours give causally_open (PushUp.causallyOpen_of_chronalNeighbours, LadderLocal.lean:350; #check type PushUp -> ChronalNeighbours -> CausallyOpen), and the space is not causally open. The disclosed first half at M (chronalMembrane_lt_le_top) is true: from Rbar the chronology lands in R, and le never leaves R.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/7-not-plain
labels.notes: chronalMembrane_not_causallyPlain states the negation of Causal.Causality.CausallyPlain. It goes through causal_ladder with pushUp_of_causallyPlain_of_absolutelyMinimal: [T1Space M] -> AbsolutelyMinimal -> CausallyPlain -> PushUp (DeuxPushup.lean:217, #check). The T1 instance of R x R is found. A direct check agrees. At a membrane point m, J+(m) is the closed Minkowski cone, so its interior holds left points of the open cone such as m + (1, 2). The closure of I+(m) = I+_Mink(m) cap R does not reach them.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/8-time-reversal
labels.notes: The positives transfer through the library's dual_* iffs: dual_chronalNeighbours, dual_causallyArcConnectedOn, dual_isCausal, dual_stronglyCausalOpen, dual_causallyCompact. The time function is oneWayMembrane_dual_hasTimeFunction, by defeq. The dual is not causally open in the future, which is the membrane's past failure. The other negations come by causal_ladder on C.dual from that one fact (kb/0091): not LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, CausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpen, PushUp, LocallyPushUp, CausallyPlain or GloballyHyperbolic. These match the direct facts: no open set about a membrane point is causally open in the past for the membrane. The dual is causally open in the past, since dual.dual is chronalMembrane by rfl; this is said in the REPORT and not stated as a theorem, which is enough. chronalMembrane_dual_absolutelyMinimalOn gives the either-reading form.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal/9-separation
labels.notes: In a probe I restated both conjunctions with the ladder's lean constants written out in full (Causal.Causality.* applied to chronalMembrane or chronalMembrane.dual, and Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal to .toPrecausality). `with_reducible exact chronalMembrane_separates` and `... dual_separates` both check. chronalMembrane_separates has 18 conjuncts. The 11 positives are ChronalNeighbours, AbsolutelyMinimal, CausallyArcConnected, Tarentin, CausallyOpenFuture, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, IsCausal, StronglyCausalOpen, StronglyCausal, HasTimeFunction and CurvesExtend. The 7 negations are CausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpen, PushUp, LocallyPushUp, CausallyPlain, CausallyCompact and GloballyHyperbolic. The dual has the 9 positives without future openness and the 9 negations listed in the REPORT. The keeper's 'from' lists equal the positive conjuncts exactly. The space is R x R, which is T2 and second countable, hence on the ambient, so no space key is needed. exists_chronalNeighbours_absolutelyMinimal_not_locallyPushUp: there is C : Causality (R x R) with (for all W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W), CAC, CN, COF, not LPU, not CP, not LCO and not dual.COF (gluing-reading form). The three _bare forms negate universal implications over Causality (R x R) from CAC and CN. One instance refutes each of them. not_causallyOpen_of_chronalNeighbours_bare refutes '-> LocallyCausallyOpen', which is stronger than its name and matches its docstring ('not even locally'). One nit, not a finding: the REPORT's load_bearing says the 7 entries, read forwards only, settle the pairs 'one to one'. Forward-only, the dual's to = locally_causally_open_future settles 4 chronal_neighbours pairs (CO, COF, LCO, LCOF), not 2. Read backwards, as the committed tool does, it settles all 7, as the REPORT says.

findings.what: Label 1-causality is marked (marked: true, with ** in the docstring), but its hypothesis row says 'carried, in a reading'. kb/0006 leaves a label that is proved 'in a reading' unmarked. This repeats finding 3 of T-abs-one-way-membrane/AUDIT-1.json, which the master graduated with the wording unchanged. The reading concerns the planner's informal 'timelike curves in U that respect the membrane', not a paper statement. It is disclosed in the SCOPE and in labels[0].questions. I re-derived the equivalence of polygonal chains with timelike curves respecting the membrane (inscribed polygon plus affinity of x1), so the mark is substantively warranted.
findings.fix: Write 'carried (polygonal chains of future timelike segments; equal to the curve reading, argued in SCOPE)', or let the master record the convention once for both membrane modules.

findings.what: The note says 'With the planner's untilted diagonal v - (e, e) the past step from a membrane point would fail the side condition'. The mathematics is right: at a membrane point both diagonal neighbours fail, the future one as well. But the roadmap block (title and evidence, programme/roadmap.toml:925-937) contains no diagonal pair, and the planner only says chronal neighbours hold. The notes field itself words it as 'a naive reading of the sketch'. As written, it credits the planner with a mistake the planner's text does not contain.
findings.fix: Say 'the diagonal pair v -/+ (e, e) would fail at a membrane point (both of them)'. If the pair came from the closer's dispatch, cite the dispatch.

findings.what: The proposal says the naive condition a in R -> b in R 'is open in neither end'. Under the proposal's own criterion (the premise set closed, the conclusion set open), the naive condition does have an open conclusion. Moving the end keeps it, since R is open. Only the start fails: a start on the membrane has starts in R arbitrarily near it, and R is not closed. The module's own docstring of chronalMembraneStep.eventually_left (:136-140) says this correctly. A kb entry would carry the inaccurate version.
findings.fix: Say that the naive condition passes the end test (R open) and fails the start test (R not closed: a start on the membrane has starts in R arbitrarily near it).
